summary.text: Michael Guest has represented Mississippi's 3rd Congressional District since 2019. A Rankin County resident, he was a prosecutor in Madison and Rankin counties for more than a decade and was elected district attorney there in 2007. In the 119th Congress he chairs the House Committee on Ethics and the Homeland Security Committee's Border Security and Enforcement subcommittee and sits on Appropriations.

paragraphs.text: Guest is a Rankin County resident and a graduate of Brandon High School, according to his official biography. He earned a bachelor's degree from Mississippi State University in 1992 and a J.D. from the University of Mississippi in 1995; his congressional biography describes the Mississippi State degree as being in accounting.
He served as an assistant district attorney for Madison and Rankin counties from 1995 to 2007 and was elected district attorney of the two counties in 2007.

Guest won the 2018 general election, defeating Michael Evans (D), to succeed retiring Rep. Gregg Harper (R). He is serving his fourth term, and his official biography says he was the first Republican freshman in the 116th Congress to pass a bill, the Terrorist and Foreign Fighter Travel Exercise Act of 2019, which was signed into law.

In the 119th Congress he chairs the House Committee on Ethics and the Border Security and Enforcement subcommittee of the House Committee on Homeland Security, and he sits on the House Committee on Appropriations, including its Homeland Security, Energy and Water Development, and Military Construction-Veterans Affairs subcommittees.

According to his official biography, Guest is a member of the Rankin County Bar Association and the Mississippi Bar Association, teaches a Sunday school class at Brandon Baptist Church, and is married with two sons.
